ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the left side is an air region, marked η = 120π Ω; the lower left corner is marked incident wave |E0| = 10 V/m, Freq = 1.1 GHz. The wave is normally incident from left to right onto the gray dielectric region on the right side. In the gray dielectric, μr = 1 − j2 and εr = 1 − j2 are marked, and the required |E| is marked at a position 10 cm from the interface inside the dielectric. Reasoning calculation: Medium 1 is air, η1 = 120π Ω. The intrinsic impedance of medium 2 is η2 = η0 sqrt(μr/εr). Since in the figure μr = εr = 1 − j2, μr/εr = 1, therefore η2 = η0 = 120π Ω. The interface impedance is matched, the reflection coefficient Γ = (η2 − η1)/(η2 + η1) = 0, so the electric-field amplitude transmitted to the dielectric boundary is still 10 V/m. The free-space wave number k0 = 2πf/c = 2π(1.1e9)/(3e8) ≈ 23.04 rad/m. According to the method specified in the problem, the propagation constant γ = j k0 sqrt(μr εr) = j k0(1 − j2) = 2k0 + j k0, so the attenuation constant α = 2k0 ≈ 46.08 Np/m. After entering the dielectric 0.10 m, the electric-field amplitude |E| = 10 exp(−αd) = 10 exp(−46.08 × 0.10) ≈ 10 exp(−4.608) ≈ 0.0997 V/m, approximately 0.1 V/m.

method.method_draft: First describe the figure: a normally incident plane wave in air enters a gray dielectric; the figure lists ηair = 120π Ω, μr = εr = 1 − j2, |E0| = 10 V/m, f = 1.1 GHz, and asks for |E| at a point 10 cm inside. Then compute η2 and the interface transmission coefficient. Because μr/εr = 1, the dielectric impedance equals air impedance, so there is no reflection and the transmitted boundary amplitude is 10 V/m. Compute k0 = 2π(1.1 GHz)/c and α from γ = jk0√(μrεr)=jk0(1−j2), giving α = 2k0. Finally multiply the boundary field by e^{-α(0.10)} to obtain about 0.1 V/m.
